results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Nebius Raised Cloud GPU Prices Up to 21% — The Local Inference Math Just Shifted | GeniusTechLab
highlights:
October 26, 2026 · 7 min read · AI Hardware

Cloud GPU compute just got more expensive again. Effective October 1, 2026, Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) raised its on-demand rates across all four of its current Nvidia platforms by roughly 12–21% — the second major increase inside a year. The H100 NVLink jumped from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, the H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, and the flagship B300 now rents at $9.50 an hour. On its face it's one neocloud's price list. In reality it's the cleanest price signal yet that on-demand AI compute is being repriced as a scarce utility — and that shifts the break-even math toward hardware you own.

...

## The October 2026 rate card, line by line

Nebius publishes its list pricing openly, which makes the change easy to audit straight from the company's official price page. The on-demand, pay-as-you-go numbers that took effect October 1:

| GPU platform | Before | After (Oct 1, 2026) | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 NVLink | $3.85 / GPU-hr | $4.50 / GPU-hr | ~+17% |
| H200 NVLink | $4.50 / GPU-hr | $5.40 / GPU-hr | +20% |
| B300 | ~$7.85 / GPU-hr | $9.50 / GPU-hr | ~+21% |

Read together with independent EU cloud price trackers — which put the median H200 rental up roughly 25% year-over-year — the direction is unambiguous. And note the shape of the increase: it's the spread between committed and on-demand pricing that's widening, not demand cooling. On-demand is becoming the premium product; the discount goes to whoever signs a contract.

...

Three forces are compounding. First, HBM is the binding constraint: Rubin Ultra's memory demands and the broader AI buildout have absorbed the wafer and HBM supply that would normally flow into next-gen accelerators — the same dynamic inflating the DDR5 prices on our memory crisis tracker.

...

For neoclouds, the choice between reprice and ration isn't really a choice. When allocation is scarce, you raise the rate for the customers who didn't commit. That's mechanically what happened on October 1 — and with enterprise inference demand still compounding quarter over quarter, the pressure is structural, not cyclical.

...

The bottom line: October's hike didn't change what AI costs — it changed who pays the shortage tax. Committed buyers and hardware owners are largely insulated; on-demand renters absorb the increase in full. As Rubin and MI450 supply land through 2027 most analysts expect rates to flatten, not roll back. Until then, every month of continuous on-demand inference is a month of equity you didn't build. If cloud is still your default, this is the quarter to price the alternative honestly.

results.title: Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another. | Compute Stacker
results.author: Compute Stacker
highlights:
Four pricing changes in eight days at one provider. None at another.

What actually happened on H100 rate cards this month:

- October 1: Nebius raised on-demand H100 from $3.85 to $4.50, up 16.9%, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50, up 21%. Its second increase in three months.
- October 7: AWS reserved Capacity Blocks moved to $5.970 per H100 accelerator-hour, the same rate across twelve regions.
- October 8: Nebius switched preemptible H100, H200, B200, B300 and RTX PRO 6000 to dynamic spot pricing. The published $2.15 became a floor of $0.79, with prices that can change every 15 minutes, including during a run, capped one cent below the on-demand rate.
- CoreWeave's HGX H100 node stayed at $49.24, or $6.16 per GPU.

Five things a headline rate doesn't tell you:

1. Per GPU or per node. CoreWeave, Oracle, Google and Azure sell H100s as 8-GPU nodes. If you need three, you pay for eight.
2. Volume rules. AWS charges $5.970 whether you take one GPU or eight. Lambda charges $4.29 for one and $3.99 each for eight.
3. Region. Nebius's H100 is in eu-north1 only. Google's 8-GPU H100 varies about 30% between its cheapest and priciest regions.
4. Purchase type. On-demand, spot, reserved and committed can differ by more than 3x on the same chip, with completely different reliability.
5. What's bundled. Lambda and CoreWeave list free egress. AWS charges about $0.09 per GB after an allowance.

The practical rule: compare the same purchase type, in the same region, at the same granularity, on the day you're buying. Anything else is comparing two different products.

results.title: Are 200 Neoclouds About to Collapse? Our Data Says No
results.author: Chad Everett Harris
highlights:
The increases were not random. In particular, short-term and flexible prices moved first: spot, serverless, capacity blocks and monthly reservations. By contrast, one-year and three-year reserved prices did not move. That pattern is what you would expect if buyers who need capacity now are bidding for it.

One seller makes the point clearly, since Verda reprices its GPUs every few days. Its H100 on-demand price rose from $3.25 an hour on September 11 to $4.56 on October 25, an increase of 40%. 3 In fact, all 23 of the Verda prices we track went up.

...

Others moved too, although less sharply. For example, Runpod’s tracked prices rose a median of about 14%. AWS capacity blocks rose a median of 7.5%, while individual Nebius and Crusoe prices rose 20% and 15%. 3 Meanwhile, Azure, Google, CoreWeave and Lambda left their tracked prices unchanged.

...

Here is the number that made me rethink this market. Our latest check found 31 standard on-demand prices for an NVIDIA H100. 3 The cheapest was $1.99 an hour, while the most expensive was $12.29. The median was $4.09. Our GPU page, which also counts calendar-mode and serverless rates, shows 38 on-demand prices with a typical price of $4.35. 9

...

None of this means every neocloud can simply raise prices. In fact, a price increase fails when the product is interchangeable, when delivery is unreliable or when the customer can switch to a cheaper credible option tomorrow.

It also fails when the customer’s own AI economics are weak. If an enterprise cannot make money from its workload, a higher rate just speeds up churn. For that reason, choosing customers is part of survival. Well-funded model companies, institutions with dedicated budgets and time-critical workloads can carry a premium, while speculative buyers usually cannot.

results.title: H100 Index Up 44% From Dec Low; Spot at $0.79 | alfw.ai
highlights:
- Silicon Data's H100 Rental Index rose from $2.00 per GPU-hour on December 9, 2025 to $2.88 on October 24, 2026, up 44% from its December low.
- Nebius raised posted on-demand prices effective October 1, 2026, by about 17% to 21% across H100, H200, B200 and B300, while leaving its RTX PRO 6000 and L40S rates unchanged.
- Runpod's displayed Secure Cloud H100 SXM rate is $3.99 per hour, up from $3.29.
- In Silicon Data's October 8–16 spot study, Nebius's H100 spot quotes averaged $0.80 and sat at a $0.79 floor in one region, against a $2.33 market spot median: quoted prices diverged across rental arrangements.
- More than half of tracked spot price series never changed price during the nine days; Silicon Data lists infrequent repricing, customer preferences, operating costs and thin trading as possible explanations.

...

The posted lists moved the same way. Nebius, the Amsterdam-based neocloud, repriced its on-demand table effective October 1. Its posted on-demand prices, in USD per GPU-hour, before and from October 1: H100 $3.85 to $4.50 (+16.9%); H200 $4.50 to $5.40 (+20.0%); B200 $7.15 to $8.50 (+18.9%); B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (+21.0%). The current rates are on Nebius's own pricing page; the before-and-after schedule rests on two independent tracker reads of that page on October 1 and October 8, with IntuitionLabs displaying the same $4.50 H100 rate from October 1. The increases were selective: the RTX PRO 6000 stayed at $1.80, and the L40S lines, at $1.55 and $1.82, did not move. Selective increases of that shape are what a provider posts when particular cards are drawing demand; a shortage of specific cards is one possible explanation, not the only one. Runpod moved at a smaller scale: its Secure Cloud H100 SXM rate is displayed at $3.99, up from $3.29 earlier in the autumn.

...

Spot capacity is the interruptible kind, sold cheap because the provider can take it back. Across sellers, and excluding Nebius, the H100 spot median over those nine days was $2.33 per GPU-hour, with quotes from $1.38 to $4.49. Nebius had just moved its preemptible prices to a dynamic system that resets as often as every 15 minutes, with a ceiling one cent below on-demand. Its H100 quotes averaged $0.80, sat at the $0.79 floor for most of the window, in a single region, eu-north1, and were the cheapest quote in the market on all nine days. The newest card behaved differently: the B300 spot median was $4.95, and Nebius's B300 quotes rose through the week.

Silicon Data says Nebius supplied the quote data for the study and that the companies were discussing broader data sharing. Nebius did not review or approve the analysis. The reported figures are quoted prices, not evidence of completed rentals.

results.title: GPU rental prices are rising in 2026 — the dated evidence | GPUJournal
highlights:
### The verdict

- Nebius — Raised rates across the board. H100 SXM now $4.50/hr.
- RunPod Secure — Raised Secure Cloud rates. H200 $4.59 → $5.29/hr (▲ 15%); RTX 4090 $0.74 → $0.89/hr (▲ 20%).
- Verda — Three rises in four days — all nine rose on Oct 23 and Oct 26; seven of nine rose again on Oct 24. H100 SXM $4.34 → $4.61/hr (▲ 6.2%).
- The cheapest offers — No movement in our records. The best verified H100 offer is still $2.25/hr.

## The evidence, date by date

Every rise below was read on the provider's own published pricing page on both sides of the change — the before figure and the after figure, each with its date. That is the standard our Price Watch applies to every entry. October 1 — Nebius raises across the board: Nebius lifted its on-demand rates at the start of October, and our board carries the post-rise rates (H100 $4.50/hr, H200 $5.40/hr, B200 $8.50/hr, verified Oct 19 and re-read unchanged Oct 26). October 14 — RunPod Secure goes up: RTX 4090 rose from $0.74 to $0.89/hr (▲ 20%) and H200 from $4.59 to $5.29/hr (▲ 15%) on RunPod's Secure Cloud; both rates were re-read on RunPod's own page on Oct 24 and Oct 26 — unchanged since the rise. October 23, 24 and 26 — Verda rises three times in four days: all nine Verda GPUs rose on Oct 23 and again on Oct 26, and seven of the nine rose on Oct 24 as well (A100 40GB and L40S held that day) — the full table is below. We are not the only ones seeing it: a third-party analysis published Oct 21, 2026 found H100 prices up at six of seven specialist GPU clouds during 2026. Our own records cover October in daily detail; the direction agrees.

### Verda — three rises in four days, in full

All figures USD per GPU per hour, read on verda.com/pricing on each date shown.

| GPU | Oct 22 | Oct 23 | Oct 24 | Oct 26 | 4-day move |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $4.34 | $4.51 | $4.56 | $4.61 | ▲ 6.2% |
| H200 | $5.66 | $5.89 | $5.95 | $6.01 | ▲ 6.2% |
| B200 | $8.07 | $8.36 | $8.44 | $8.52 | ▲ 5.6% |
| B300 | $10.28 | $10.69 | $10.80 | $10.91 | ▲ 6.1% |
| GB300 | $11.82 | $12.29 | $12.42 | $12.55 | ▲ 6.2% |
| A100 80GB | $2.07 | $2.13 | $2.15 | $2.16 | ▲ 4.3% |
| A100 40GB | $1.52 | $1.56 | $1.56 | $1.58 | ▲ 3.9% |
| RTX PRO 6000 | $2.40 | $2.49 | $2.52 | $2.54 | ▲ 5.8% |
| L40S | $1.77 | $1.81 | $1.81 | $1.83 | ▲ 3.4% |

### The half that has not moved

Against those rises, the cheapest verified offers on our board did not move at all during the week of Oct 19–26:

| GPU | Best verified offer | Provider | Oct 19 → Oct 26 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $2.25/hr | TensorDock (8-GPU minimum) | — unchanged |
| H200 | $3.59/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| B200 | $5.98/hr | RunPod Community | — unchanged |
| RTX 4090 | $0.20/hr | nafnaf | — unchanged |
| A100 80GB | $1.09/hr | Thunder Compute | — unchanged |

Read the terms before you chase the floor — minimum commitments and community-cloud availability differ from list-rate clouds. But the fact stands: on Oct 26 you could still rent an H100 for roughly half the rate a rising list price asks ($2.25 vs $4.50–$4.61). Rising list prices have not pulled the floor up — yet.

...

GPUJournal reads providers' own published pricing pages and banks the figures at every check. The checks behind this page fell on Oct 19, 22, 23, 24 and 26, 2026 — there are gaps between them, so the October rises are documented check by check rather than day by day. A price change we catch in our own checks is only reported when both the before and after figures were seen on the provider's own page, each with its date; that is how the Verda and RunPod rises above were verified. The Nebius rise of Oct 1, 2026 is different: it predates our records and was an announced rise, so we did not bank both sides of it ourselves — we verified the post-rise rates on Nebius's own page (checked Oct 19, re-read unchanged Oct 26) and report it as announced. And a price a provider merely states about itself never appears on our board as a verified price. Where a provider's pages state figures we cannot ... , Price Watch reports them labelled as stated — which is how disagreements get ... rather than hidden: on Oct 26, Spheron's pages stated the same H100 at $2.64 on some pages and $2.98 on others, and we report the disagreement rather than pick a number.

results.title: H100 rental prices are spiking even as Wall Street worries about an AI bubble - Startup Fortune
results.author: Dave Barr
highlights: Nebius raised its on-demand H100 rate from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on October 1, 2026, a roughly 17% jump. Runpod's Secure Cloud H100 SXM rate climbed from $3.29 in early September to $3.99 by mid-October. Across the market, Silicon Data's H100 Rental Index, launched in May 2025 as the first daily benchmark of its kind for GPU rental pricing, rose from $2 per GPU-hour on December 9, 2025, to $2.88 on October 24, 2026, a 44% increase.

results.title: B200 deals top Nebius list price; only Ornn's index shows it | SecondSource
highlights:
## At a glance

1. Ornn, a company that publishes a GPU rental-price index built from completed deals, puts B200 at US$9.70 per GPU-hour, up 20.65% in a month and above the US$8.50 on-demand list price of Nebius, a cloud provider that rents out GPUs. On the same index, H100 rose only 6.32%.

...

### 1. [Today] (index, October 25) On Ornn's transaction index, B200 and H200 rental prices rose more than 20% in a month and passed a provider's list price, while H100 lagged

Ornn compiles a GPU rental-price index from completed deals, and the October 25 reading shows B200 and H200 rental prices up more than 20% in a month, to above the on-demand list price of Nebius, a cloud provider that specializes in renting GPUs. H100 rental prices rose only 6.32% in a month on the same index and still sit below the Nebius list price; transaction prices so far come from Ornn alone. Our read: list price is not a ceiling on B200 and H200 rents, at least among the deals Ornn records.

Why it matters: Buyers who budget B200 and H200 rentals against provider list prices may be underestimating what completed deals now cost. H100 deals still sit below list. The evidence so far is one index, Ornn's.
